stateOfPlay: Eisenkot's Yashar leads Likud 23 to 20, and neither bloc is close: the Netanyahu bloc sits at 52, the change bloc at 51. What the arithmetic now shows is starker than a gap. Of every possible combination of these parties, not one reaches 61 without crossing a line someone has already drawn — because every change-bloc leader except Yair Golan has declared he will not rely on Ra'am, and Eisenkot has ruled out both Netanyahu and the far right. That is why Eisenkot has begun preparing a minority government of 58 or 59 seats, governing with Arab parties' support from outside rather than inside. Yoav Segelovich joining Ra'am's list is aimed squarely at making the inside version thinkable again.
raamNote: Ra'am is the hinge, and every change-bloc leader except Yair Golan has said he will not rely on it — Bennett explicitly ruling out a repeat 'post-October 7', Eisenkot rejecting Abbas's offer to join outright. Those pledges have been broken before: Bennett signed one on live television in 2021 and brought Ra'am into government months later. Yoav Segelovich, a former Yesh Atid MK, now runs on Ra'am's list — the first Jewish figure to do so, and aimed at exactly this objection.
_outlooksComment: Odds are YOUR editorial call — these are a starting point, not a calculation. The seat totals beside each are computed live from polls.json.

outlooks.label: Eisenkot, with Ra'am and Hendel
outlooks.why: The only combination that reaches 61 on current numbers, and it does so exactly. Hendel is the realistic partner here — his refusal to sit with Shas and UTJ over the draft leaves him little room on the right — but it asks Beyachad and Hendel to accept a government resting on Ra'am. Segelovich joining Ra'am's list was aimed at precisely that objection.

outlooks.label: Another election
outlooks.why: The Netanyahu bloc tops out at 52 even with Winter's four seats, and there is no ninth seat available to it that isn't Arab-majority. If the change bloc cannot settle on Ra'am, nobody forms a government and Israel votes again.

outlooks.label: A unity government, without Netanyahu
outlooks.why: Comfortably past 61 and blocked by one man: most of these partners have ruled out serving under Netanyahu, not under Likud. A Likud leadership change would rewrite the arithmetic overnight.

wildCardNote: The wild card is Yoaz Hendel's The Reservists, now clearing the threshold at four seats after merging with Yaron Zelekha's New Economic Party. It sits squarely between the blocs and could join either, but its refusal to sit with the ultra-Orthodox over the draft closes off the most natural path on the right — which is why the change bloc's only route to 61 runs through it.

presets.label: Netanyahu bloc at full stretch
presets.note: Even with Winter's new party, the bloc tops out in the mid-50s. There is no further seat available to it that is not Arab-majority.

presets.label: Unity — needs a new Likud leader
presets.note: Comfortably past 61 on the numbers, and irrelevant while Netanyahu leads Likud: Bennett, Lapid and Lieberman have all ruled out serving under him. This is a scenario about Likud's leadership, not about the arithmetic.
